How a request reaches this site

Each column is one party. Time moves downward, the same way a TCP handshake is drawn. The edge function gate-ai-access runs on every request after TLS, before any Jekyll file is sent. The Node functions run only when their URL is called.

1. Opening the connection

A human and an agent do the same three handshakes. DNS answers with a Netlify edge IP. The article is not involved yet.

sequenceDiagram
  participant C as Human client
  participant A as AI agent
  participant D as DNS
  participant N as Netlify edge
  participant S as Server

  C->>D: What is the IP of dheeraj-work.netlify.app?
  D-->>C: A Netlify edge IP
  C->>N: TCP SYN
  N-->>C: TCP SYN-ACK
  C->>N: TCP ACK
  C->>N: TLS ClientHello
  N-->>C: TLS certificate and keys
  Note over C,N: The connection is encrypted. No page has been sent yet.

2. A human opens a blog post

The first response is decided on the edge. The Jekyll file stays unread until the reader cookie exists.

sequenceDiagram
  participant C as Human client
  participant A as AI agent
  participant D as DNS
  participant N as Netlify edge
  participant S as Server

  C->>N: GET /2025/05/13/why-ola-is-building-its-own-llms-krutrim
  Note over N: User-Agent looks like a browser. Sec-Fetch-Mode is navigate. No cookie. No payment token.
  N-->>C: 402 challenge page
  Note over S: The article file is not read.
  C->>N: POST /api/reader-unlock after JavaScript runs
  N-->>C: Set-Cookie dw_reader
  C->>N: GET the same post, with the cookie
  N->>S: Cookie is valid, so fetch the HTML
  S-->>N: Article HTML
  N-->>C: 200 article
  N->>S: POST /api/track as human, status 200

3. An agent wants the same post

Reading /llms.txt returns the price and the wallet. It does not unlock the post.

sequenceDiagram
  participant C as Human client
  participant A as AI agent
  participant D as DNS
  participant N as Netlify edge
  participant S as Server

  A->>N: GET /llms.txt
  N->>S: Open path, fetch the file
  S-->>N: Payment terms
  N-->>A: 200 llms.txt
  Note over A: Reading this file does not unlock posts.
  A->>N: GET /2025/05/13/why-ola-is-building-its-own-llms-krutrim
  Note over N: User-Agent matches Claude, GPTBot, or another blocked agent.
  N-->>A: 402 Payment Required
  Note over S: The article file is not read.
  N->>S: POST /api/track as AI agent, status 402
  A->>N: POST /api/verify-payment with txHash
  N->>S: Check the Base USDC transfer
  S-->>N: accessToken
  N-->>A: 200 accessToken
  A->>N: GET the post with Authorization Bearer token
  N->>S: Token is valid, so fetch the HTML
  S-->>N: Article HTML
  N-->>A: 200 article

4. Which function runs, and which request hits the edge

Every URL hits gate-ai-access first. /api/reader-unlock is handled inside that edge function. The other /api URLs are separate functions, and the edge lets them through because /api/ is an open path. GET /api/bot-rules runs only when the edge’s 15-second rule cache is cold.

sequenceDiagram
  participant C as Client
  participant E as Edge gate-ai-access
  participant R as Function bot-rules
  participant T as Function track
  participant M as Function analytics
  participant F as Jekyll file in _site

  C->>E: Any GET or POST, after TCP and TLS
  alt Path is / /about /talks /projects /llms.txt /assets
    E->>F: context.next reads the static file
    F-->>E: 200 file
    E-->>C: 200 file
    E->>T: POST /api/track kind and path
    Note over T: track.mjs writes the visit to Netlify Blobs
  else Path is a post and the client is a human with no cookie
    E-->>C: 402 HTML challenge, written by the edge
    C->>E: POST /api/reader-unlock
    Note over E: Still the edge function. No Node function runs.
    E-->>C: Set-Cookie dw_reader
    C->>E: GET the post again with the cookie
    E->>F: context.next
    F-->>E: Article HTML
    E-->>C: 200 article
    E->>T: POST /api/track human 200
  else Path is a post and the User-Agent is a blocked agent
    E->>R: GET /api/bot-rules if the 15s cache is empty
    R-->>E: allowed or blocked for that name
    E-->>C: 402 JSON, or 402 HTML if it looks like a browser
    Note over F: The article file is not read.
    E->>T: POST /api/track AI agent 402
  else Path is a post and the User-Agent is Googlebot or Bingbot
    E->>F: context.next, search is allowed
    F-->>E: Article HTML
    E-->>C: 200 article
    E->>T: POST /api/track search 200
  else Browser opens /analytics/
    E->>F: context.next, this page is not a post
    F-->>E: analytics.html
    E-->>C: 200 page
    C->>E: GET /api/analytics
    Note over E: Open path, so the edge does not gate it
    E->>M: analytics.mjs reads Blobs
    M-->>E: JSON counts
    E-->>C: 200 JSON
  end

5. The agent pays, then the post is accepted

The edge checks the token on the post URL itself. /api/content checks the same token again, then fetches the HTML with X-AI-Access-Bypass so the edge will pass that internal request through.

sequenceDiagram
  participant A as AI agent
  participant E as Edge gate-ai-access
  participant V as Function verify-payment
  participant B as Base
  participant K as Function content
  participant F as Jekyll file in _site

  A->>E: GET /20xx/mm/dd/post with no token
  E-->>A: 402 pay 0.01 USDC on Base to the site wallet
  A->>B: Transfer 0.01 USDC
  B-->>A: Transaction hash
  A->>E: POST /api/verify-payment { txHash }
  Note over E: /api/ is open, so the edge forwards this
  E->>V: verify-payment.mjs
  V->>B: Read the receipt and the USDC Transfer log
  B-->>V: Success, recipient, amount at least 0.01
  V-->>E: accessToken, valid 7 days
  E-->>A: 200 { ok, accessToken }

  alt Option A, same post URL
    A->>E: GET /20xx/mm/dd/post Authorization Bearer accessToken
    Note over E: tokenOk inside the edge
    E->>F: context.next
    F-->>E: Article HTML
    E-->>A: 200 article
  else Option B, content API
    A->>E: GET /api/content?path=/20xx/mm/dd/post.html Bearer accessToken
    E->>K: content.mjs
    Note over K: verifyAccessToken, then fetch the path
    K->>E: GET that post with X-AI-Access-Bypass
    Note over E: Bypass header matches the secret, so the gate steps aside
    E->>F: context.next
    F-->>E: Article HTML
    E-->>K: 200 HTML
    K-->>A: 200 article
  end
